import pandas as pd

df_list = []
has_relation_query = False

# 1. PubMed Search (Best Relevance Sorting)
if not has_relation_query:
    pmid_df = pubmed_api_search_papers(
        boolean_query_text='"Postnatal growth restriction augments oxygen-induced pulmonary hypertension"',
        top_k=10,
    )
    if pmid_df is not None and not pmid_df.empty:
        for col in ["PMID", "Title", "Journal", "Year", "Abstract"]:
            if col not in pmid_df.columns:
                pmid_df[col] = ""
        pmid_df = pmid_df[["PMID", "Title", "Journal", "Year", "Abstract"]]
        df_list.append(pmid_df)

# 2. PubTator3 Search (Entity highlighting, fallback)
pubtator_results = []
for page in range(1, 1 + 1):
    search_results = pubtator_api_search_papers(
        boolean_query_text='"Postnatal growth restriction augments oxygen-induced pulmonary hypertension"',
        relation_query=None,
        page=page,
        max_retries=3,
        max_requests_per_second=3
    )
    if search_results is not None and not search_results.empty:
        pubtator_results.append(search_results)
    else:
        break

if pubtator_results:
    pubtator_df = pd.concat(pubtator_results)
    if "Highlighted_Text" in pubtator_df.columns:
        pubtator_df = pubtator_df.rename(columns={"Highlighted_Text": "Abstract"})
    
    for col in ["PMID", "Title", "Journal", "Year", "Abstract"]:
        if col not in pubtator_df.columns:
            pubtator_df[col] = ""
    pubtator_df = pubtator_df[["PMID", "Title", "Journal", "Year", "Abstract"]]
    df_list.append(pubtator_df)

# 3. Combine, Deduplicate and Format Clean Output
if df_list:
    final_df = pd.concat(df_list).reset_index(drop=True)
    # Deduplicate by PMID, keeping the first occurrence (which guarantees PubMed relevance is maintained)
    final_df = final_df.drop_duplicates(subset=["PMID"], keep="first")
    
    # Optional: Save to CSV for persistent logging
    final_df.to_csv('/home/data4/xiangyu/BioDSA/workdir/workdir/locate_target_rat_study.csv', index=False)
    print(f"The search results are saved at '/home/data4/xiangyu/BioDSA/workdir/workdir/locate_target_rat_study.csv'")
    print(f"Total results found: {len(final_df)}\n")
    print("=" * 80)
    print("TOP RESULTS (Showing up to 15 most relevant):")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # FORMAT FOR LLM: Clean text layout rather than Markdown table
    for idx, row in final_df.head(15).iterrows():
        pmid = row.get('PMID', 'N/A')
        title = row.get('Title', 'No Title')
        journal = row.get('Journal', 'Unknown')
        year = row.get('Year', 'Unknown')
        abstract = str(row.get('Abstract', 'No Abstract Available'))
        
        # Clean abstract spaces and truncate at 1200 chars to save context window
        abstract = " ".join(abstract.split())
        if len(abstract) > 1200:
            abstract = abstract[:1200] + " ... [Truncated]"
            
        print(f"PMID: {pmid}")
        print(f"Title: {title}")
        print(f"Source: {journal} ({year})")
        print(f"Abstract: {abstract}")
        print("-" * 80)
else:
    print("No search results found. Please try again with different query. TIP: Try simpler keyword phrases.")

--- ABSTRACT ---
[BACKGROUND]: Prematurity and fetal growth restriction are risk factors for pulmonary hypertension (PH) in infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD). Neonatal rats develop PH and vascular remodeling when exposed to hyperoxia. We hypothesize that postnatal growth restriction (PNGR) due to under-nutrition increases the severity of PH induced by hyperoxia in neonatal rats.
[METHODS]: Pups were randomized at birth to litters maintained in room air or 75% oxygen (hyperoxia), together with litters of normal milk intake (10 pups) or PNGR (17 pups). After 14 d, right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH) was assessed by Fulton's index (right ventricular weight/left ventricular plus septal weight) and PH by echocardiography. Lungs were analyzed by immunohistochemistry, morphometrics, western blotting, and metabolomics.
[RESULTS]: Hyperoxia and PNGR each significantly increased pulmonary arterial pressure, RVH and pulmonary arterial medial wall thickness, and significantly decreased pulmonary vessel number. These changes were significantly augmented in pups exposed to both insults. Hyperoxia and PNGR both significantly decreased expression of proteins involved in lung development and vasodilation.
[CONCLUSION]: PNGR induces right ventricular and pulmonary vascular remodeling and augments the effects of oxygen in neonatal rats. This may be a powerful tool to investigate the mechanisms that induce PH in low-birth-weight preterm infants with BPD.
